question_bank.stem: What diagnosis replaces the early intuition that adversarial sensitivity comes mainly from nonlinear activations?

options.text: The network behaves approximately linearly enough for many small changes to accumulate.
The network ignores the input dimensions until the final softmax layer.
The network memorizes each image and therefore cannot use gradients.
The network removes semantic features before the first convolution layer.

question_bank.explanation: The instructor says the nonlinear explanation was not correct and points to near-linearity plus high dimensionality.

distractor_rationales.B: Invents an input-ignoring mechanism not discussed.
distractor_rationales.D: Moves the issue to feature removal rather than compounding perturbations.

frame_evidence.description: Slide displays the Fast Gradient Sign Method formula after the near-linearity discussion.

question_bank.stem: In the logistic-regression-style example, why can a small epsilon perturbation shift the output strongly?

options.text: It creates an epsilon-times-squared-weight term that pushes the logit direction.
It deletes the bias term so the sigmoid becomes a constant value.
It replaces the weight vector with a random Gaussian vector.
It changes the label encoding so the loss no longer applies.

question_bank.explanation: Adding epsilon times the weight vector creates a cumulative term in the logit; across dimensions, the small shifts add up.

distractor_rationales.B: The bias simplification is not the cause of the large shift.
distractor_rationales.C: The perturbation follows the weight direction, not a random vector.
distractor_rationales.D: Label encoding is not the mechanism in the derivation.

source_ref.evidence_span: It was because it created that second term, epsilon w squared,

frame_evidence.description: Slide later summarizes the same direction-of-gradient idea with the FGSM equation.

question_bank.stem: What does FGSM do in the lecture’s one-shot attack description?

options.text: It averages many random perturbations before updating the image.
It retrains the classifier parameters for one mini-batch.
It adds epsilon times the sign of the input-gradient direction.
It removes pixels with the largest absolute input value.

question_bank.explanation: FGSM is the one-shot method that perturbs x by a small epsilon in the sign direction of the loss gradient.

distractor_rationales.A: Uses random averaging rather than the gradient sign.
distractor_rationales.B: Confuses adversarial example construction with model training.
distractor_rationales.D: Uses pixel magnitude rather than gradient direction.

source_ref.evidence_span: It's called the fast gradient sign method.

frame_evidence.description: Slide explicitly shows x* = x + epsilon sign(dJ/dX).

question_bank.stem: How should a student diagnose whether an attack is white-box in this segment?

options.text: The attacker has access to the model internals needed for gradient-based techniques.
The attacker has access to a printed patch but not to model queries.
The attacker has access to labels from users but not to the classifier.
The attacker has access to clean images but not to the target class.

question_bank.explanation: The white-box/black-box distinction is about access to the model internals; FGSM-style gradients are easier in the white-box case.

distractor_rationales.B: Describes a physical artifact, not model access.
distractor_rationales.C: Mentions labels but misses model internals.
distractor_rationales.D: Mentions data access but not the attack-access distinction.

source_ref.evidence_span: a white box attack where you have access

frame_evidence.description: Formula slide depends on access to gradients with respect to the input.

question_bank.stem: Which defense best matches adversarial training as described near the end of the segment?

options.text: Mask output layers so gradients become harder to compute.
Add correctly labeled adversarial inputs to the training objective.
Reject every input that contains any high-frequency texture.
Query a black-box model until an adversarial image transfers.

question_bank.explanation: The instructor describes duplicating the loss with adversarial versions of x, such as ones generated by FGSM, while keeping the label y the same.

distractor_rationales.A: This is closer to gradient masking, not adversarial training.
distractor_rationales.C: This overstates input sanitization and uses an absolute rule.
distractor_rationales.D: This describes an attack workflow rather than a defense.
